lines.watchItem: Demand keeps running ahead of what the chain can serve, and stacked memory rather than wafer output is what caps accelerator shipments today. Added leading-edge wafer starts can therefore arrive faster than the memory available to pair with them, while tool deliveries and construction labour set how quickly new plants come online.

Advanced-packaging lines stay booked into 2027 and the reported shortfall now ranges from about 10 percent to about 20 percent, so packaging allocation still gates how much accelerator revenue can actually be realized. Which of those two readings the coming quarters confirm is the open question.

Custom accelerator programmes from cloud operators and model labs are growing far faster than merchant accelerators and are landing on leading-edge nodes, with one large in-house programme negotiating capacity for hundreds of thousands of units. The exposure is a leading-node customer base whose mix tilts away from two merchant vendors toward many smaller custom programmes, one of which has opened talks with a rival foundry at 2 nanometres.

Memory suppliers are taking a growing share of AI server profit and the leading accelerator vendor's margin is stepping down on memory cost, even as foundry prices firm across the market. Who can raise prices in this value chain now moves with memory scarcity as much as with logic capacity.

Rival packaging routes are winning named volume, including an order for more than three million bridge-packaging units for 2028 delivery, though that route has its own single fully booked capacitor supplier and is described as a better fit for custom chips than for high-bandwidth accelerators. Alongside it sits a policy exposure: prepared tariffs on finished server hardware with duty-free allowances sized to each company's fabrication investment in the United States.

The top three advanced-packaging customers hold more than 85 percent of capacity, with one of them alone at roughly 60 percent and reserving over half of the 2026 volume. A single one of them trimming orders would leave capacity that is hard to refill at short notice.
